text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Syrian President Hafez al-Assad meets Iranian Defence Minister Mohammad Forouzandeh and receives two letters from Presidnet Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
- Assad discusses with Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri the peace process and Israel's position rejecting the Madrid land-for-peace formula.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu left his consultant in Washington and did not present anything to resume peace talks on the Syrian-Israeli track.

- The Arab parliamentarian session over the future of water in the Middle East opens and head of Syrian People's Assembly (parliament) Abdel-Qadir Qaddoura says there is no alternative to a comprehensive Arab startegy to save and protect waters.
- Syrian Finance Ministry suggests 210 billion Syrian pound budget for 1997. Increase in the budget was because Syria amended the dollar price for oil exports to 35 pounds to a dollar.
- The state-owned Syrian Establishement for Post and Telephone Telecommunication agreed with a private company to invest in the public telephone cabines in Damascus and Aleppo.
- Syria has around 45 tonnes of gold owned by women and goldsmiths. Syria exported 2.5 tonnes of gold acccessories in 1996 to Gulf Arab countries, Europe and North Africa.
- Jordanian parties and personalities hold a demonstration to show solidarity with Syria's positions in the Middle East peace process.
- Egytian cabinet reviews results of the Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara's visit to Cairo.
- South Lebanon ceasefire committee met as Israel shelled villages in the south.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton says Washington ready to do anything to achieve peace between Syria and Israel. Israel's obstinacy leaves no room for the resumption of talks.
- Revenues of the free zone in the port of Lattakia, around 350 km (220 miles) north of Damascus, were around 28 million pounds in 1994.
